plainTitle: A study of more ways to speed up the 505 Dundas streetcar

sources.label: Staff report from the Director, Congestion and Network Management, Transportation Services

whatIsProposed.text: City Council asked City staff and the TTC to look into adding more measures that give the 505 Dundas streetcar priority on the road, beyond the ones already in place.

citations.quote: to investigate the feasibility and options for expanding Transit Priority Measures for the 505 Dundas streetcar outside of the currently implemented Transit Priority Measures

whatIsProposed.text: This decision asks for a study and a plan for consulting the public. It does not change any parking or turning rules.

citations.quote: such investigation to include further analysis of the 505 Dundas streetcar performance and development of an engagement plan to support future Transit Priority Measures

whatIsProposed.text: The measures already in place are longer no-stopping hours in weekday rush hours and more left-turn restrictions on Dundas Street.

citations.quote: expanding ‘No Stopping’ coverage of the AM and PM peak periods on weekdays, as well as new and expanded left-turn restrictions

why.text: The aim is to make streetcar trips shorter and more reliable.

citations.quote: to further reduce travel times and improve reliability of the Dundas streetcar for transit riders

why.text: Early results from the first measures: on the sections that were changed, trips became up to 5 minutes faster.
why.caveat: Staff say only one week of data after the changes was usable, because of diversions and patio installations.

citations.quote: These impacts reflect travel time improvements of up to 5 minutes
the only representative week of data post-implementation of TPMs was April 6 to April 12, 2026

why.text: Weekly ridership on the 505 rose by about 20% between fall 2025 and spring 2026, from about 187,000 to 224,000 a week.
why.caveat: Staff say the increase cannot be credited to the road measures alone, because streetcars also started running more often.

citations.quote: This represents a 20% increase in ridership on the 505 Dundas streetcar route.
Impacts to ridership cannot be solely attributed to the more frequent service or the TPMs impact on travel times

whoIsAffected.text: People who ride the 505 Dundas streetcar.

citations.quote: improve reliability of the Dundas streetcar for transit riders

whoIsAffected.text: People who drive, park, make deliveries or run a business on Dundas Street. The first measures changed parking and traffic rules on Dundas Street East and West, and an expansion could change more.
whoIsAffected.caveat: The record does not say which blocks or which rules a future expansion would involve.

citations.quote: permanent parking and traffic amendments to Dundas Street East and West

whoIsAffected.text: The City lists four wards for this item: 4 (Parkdale-High Park), 9 (Davenport), 10 (Spadina-Fort York) and 13 (Toronto Centre).

citations.quote: 4 - Parkdale - High Park, 9 - Davenport, 10 - Spadina - Fort York, 13 - Toronto Centre

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: Staff and the TTC are asked to come back with recommendations in the first three months of 2027.

citations.quote: to report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee with recommendations on Part 1 above in the first quarter of 2027

conditionsAndUnknowns.text: City Council made one change to the community council's version: it named the committee that must receive the report. The community council's wording only said “report back”.

citations.quote: to report back with recommendations on Part 1 above in the first quarter of 2027
That City Council amend recommendation 2 so that it reads as follows:

staff.text: Staff only asked that their report be received for information. They did not recommend expanding the measures.

citations.quote: Toronto and East York Community Council receive this report for information.

committee.text: The community council went further than staff. It recommended that City Council ask for a study of expanding the measures.

citations.quote: The Toronto and East York Community Council recommends that:

council.text: City Council approved the request for a study, and added that the report must go to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee.

citations.quote: City Council adopted this item on July 29 and 30, 2026 with amendments.

whatHappensNext.text: The report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee is due in the first quarter of 2027. The record does not say what happens after that report.
whatHappensNext.caveat: No meeting date for that report is in the record yet. When it is scheduled, the City's page for that new item will show whether you can comment or speak.

citations.quote: to report to the Infrastructure and Environment Committee with recommendations on Part 1 above in the first quarter of 2027
